client_statement:
[Panicking] OK, I’m definitely feeling anxious now! Um, what’s the point of this exposure
again? What if it doesn’t work? What if I can’t stop feeling like this? Maybe we should
stop now.
[Sad] I was feeling hopeless and didn’t want to come in today.

[Frustrated] I’m still having trouble making appointments. I either completely miss them
or end up being late. I just can’t get it together.

[Angry] I don’t like this or find it helpful. My thoughts aren’t irrational or baseless,
so I actually find it kind of invalidating and insulting.

[Frustrated] I know I said I would go to the event and start a conversation with new
people, but I only managed to say “hello” to one person.

[Angry] It’s hard to come up with goals because I’m not really sure what we’re doing in
here.
[Weeping] I’m so embarrassed. I’m an ugly crier.

[Frustrated] Whelp, the homework was another big swing and miss. Made no sense.
Can we not do that one again?
[Nervous] I don’t think I’m ready to work on this today.
[Defeated] To be honest, I wouldn’t expect you to ever really get me.

[Nervous] I guess I was expecting that we’d just talk about whatever came to my mind on
a given week.

[Frustrated] You don’t understand. I can’t do these things because I’m depressed. If I
wasn’t depressed, I could easily do these things, and I wouldn’t need to be here in the
first place.
[Curious] Geez. I don’t even know where to start in picturing my happiness.
[Hopeless] To be honest, things haven’t improved as much as I expected.

[Anxious] I want to get a job, find a new partner, lose weight, be happier and less anxious,
be more outgoing, and work on some my grief issues.
[Calm] I’m not sure what to talk about today.

[Hopeless, after completing a progress monitoring measure] I think the scores on the
measure you asked me to complete are consistent with my experience so far. It feels like
things might actually be getting worse.

[Shaking and weeping] This is not something I can get into without hysterically crying.
That’s why I avoid it.

[Angry] You seem so concerned with just finishing what’s on your list before time runs out.
I feel like I’m just a plug-and-play client!

[Ashamed] I know we talked about me having that date last week. I ended up cancelling
at the last minute. You know, I actually felt relieved.

[Angry] I think I’m done with therapy . . . things aren’t that bad, and maybe I don’t want to
change! I’ve been dealing with this my whole life and I’ve managed.
[Nervous] You’re the expert, so I’ll defer to what you think is best.

[Angry] My doctor said I have to come see you about my “anger problem.” Sometimes
when I get really angry, I lose control and hit people. I just get so angry when people say
stupid things! Are you sure that you will be able to help me with this?
[Impatient] How long will it take for this to work? I don’t have a lot of time or money.
[Curious] So, what’s our agenda for today?
[Very anxious] I feel like I’m going to have a panic attack or faint!

[Irritated] When we work through these thought records, it’s not hard to come up with
alternative evidence and thoughts, but it feels artificial and doesn’t really make me
feel better.
[Frustrated] I don’t expect this assignment to help.

[Anxious] I have a hard time with organization, so I’m worried about doing all of the
homework correctly

[Tearing up] I don’t even know if I’m getting any better in here. I mean, I’ve been in therapy
for weeks and I feel the same.
[Pleased] I feel like I’m getting the hang of objective monitoring.

[Sad] I guess I’m feeling hopeless. A part of me wants to change, but another part is afraid
of who I’ll be if I change too much.
[Agitated] I’m too swamped; I don’t think I’ll have the time to do any homework.

[Angry] You’re the worst. You keep asking me to interpret the situation in different ways,
like my perspective is always wrong. It’s like you’re calling me a liar. My last therapist would
not have called me a liar.

[Depressed] I wasn’t able to do the trauma homework. I’ve been feeling more depressed
and sleeping a lot. I’ve been late to work a few days this week.
[Sad, withdrawn] I just don’t know what to say or do anymore . . . to you—or anyone.
[Withdrawn] I’m not sure where to start, or what to prioritize on today’s agenda. Sorry.
[Anxious] I don’t really know anyone who will be at this party. I know I’ll be miserable.

[Irritated] The agenda sounds fine, I suppose. I don’t know. I don’t think this is working,
so I’m not sure it matters.

[Irritated] I can’t commit to coming in here each week. My schedule is unpredictable,
and I don’t have a car.

[Angry] Now you just seem to be playing a psychologist . . . like the cliché ones on TV.
But I guess you’re the expert, so tell me what’s next please.
[Frustrated] I don’t know why I keep blowing up at people. I just do.
[Challenging] Are you all here today? No offense, doc, but your mind seems elsewhere.

[Nervous] I know that the plan was to talk about exposure today, but something’s come up
that I’d like to talk about first.

[Happy] I did what you suggested about my thoughts, and it really helped in the moment.
Every time I had a negative thought, I just told myself the opposite.
[Anxious] I don’t think I want to do any exposure.

[Irritated] My mother was trying to remind me to “check in” on my thoughts and breathing
yesterday. So annoying. People are always trying to solve my problems without possibly
being able to understand what I’m going through.

[Hopeless] Before being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, I loved hiking. I’m devastated
because nothing is going to replace that. It’s all over.

[Helpless] I was abused when I was a child, and recently I can’t stop thinking about it.
My boyfriend tries to help me be positive, but I can’t stop feeling depressed. Sometimes
I think it would be easier for everyone if I was dead.

[Anxious] Whenever I have trouble motivating to do the homework, I think of how happy
I will feel telling you that I did it. Your approval means everything to me. I honestly think
you’re the best therapist I’ve ever met.

[Impatient] You talk about the importance of thoughts . . . I’m already very aware of my
negative thoughts.

[Excited] I found this article about a breakthrough medication for anxiety, and it seems like
something I could try.
[Irritated] I don’t think this is going to work, so I’m not sure setting goals matters.

[Anxious] I’m uneasy about doing the homework, living with my extended family in such
a small place. It makes me uncomfortable.

[Anxious] I guess I haven’t brought up religion in here yet; I’ve been unsure about
doing that.

[Sad] I think our sessions have been very helpful. However, my depression is getting worse.
On my drive to this session today. I pictured myself driving off a bridge. It honestly felt like
a relief to imagine not having to work so hard to feel better anymore.
[Confused] I’m not sure I understand how talking about my feelings will help.
[Nervous] I don’t think I’m ready for working on this today.
[Sad, failing to make eye contact] I guess I don’t deserve better.
[Frustrated] I don’t think I can commit to coming here every week.
[Anxious] I know the job interview is going to go poorly; they always do.
[Nervous] I just don’t want to feel anxious anymore. I’m tired of it.

[Frustrated] I don’t like it when you ask me if I have “catastrophic thoughts.” Aren’t
catastrophes reserved for wars and natural disasters? So, no, I don’t think I catastrophize.
Please don’t ask again.

[Afraid] I’ve had bad experiences in therapy before. My last therapist tried to make me talk
about and visualize my past traumas. I ended up in the hospital! How can I know that I can
trust you?
[Anxious] I’m not ready to try the next item on my exposure hierarchy.

[Angry] I mean, of course, relaxation would be nice, but who can shut off their mind like
that? I’m not even sure I’d want to . . . I might just end up lazy and complacent! I don’t
know . . . it’s so frustrating.
[Curious] Is this approach helpful for people like me?

[Anxious] I don’t think I’m ready to do all of what you’re asking me to do before the
next session.
[Sad] I’m a total failure.

[Curious] I read an article on the internet that a new energy-healing technique can help
people 10 times faster than CBT and is easy for therapists to learn. I brought a printout of
the article with instructions. Can we talk about possibly trying that today?

[Anxious] I’ve been working hard on keeping my drinking under control, but it’s hard.
I’m kind of nervous because my friend insists on having his birthday party at the bar
this weekend.

[Angry] You just need goals to write down for the insurance companies so you get paid
for this.
[Irritated] This week has been terrible, and I don’t feel like talking today.

[Disgusted, looking away] Ugh. Ahh. That is disgusting! I am not looking at that or
touching it!
[Impatient] I think there’s a problem with my brain and I might just need medication.
[Agitated] Honestly, my main problem is my partner.

[Angry] I don’t think you really care about me! You just pretend to like me because it’s
your job!
[Agitated] Wow. You won’t believe what happened this week. It’s a really long story . . .

[Ashamed] Umm. After being sober for 6 months, as you know . . . I drank this week. I feel
like such a failure.

[Ambivalent] I apologize for missing sessions, but I just wasn’t sure about coming back.
I’m not convinced I need to change all that much—if anything.
[Withdrawn] Honestly, I don’t know about CBT . . . almost seems a bit condescending.

[Pessimistic] I know I agreed to this approach, and I understand what we’re trying to do
here, but I’m starting to doubt it’s a good fit.
[Curious] OK, what do we do now that we’ve created an exposure hierarchy?
[Frustrated] I don’t like this breathing stuff. The experience monitoring was more helpful.

[Dismissive] I didn’t do the homework. It didn’t seem like it was that important, to be
honest.
[Angry] You’re telling me that if my partner died, I should be fine with it?!
[Flustered] Sorry I’m so late. I had the wrong time in my calendar.

[Reluctant] I have to admit to not doing the homework. I don’t think I “distort” my
thoughts any more than the next person, so the assignment seemed a bit, well, silly—
pardon my bluntness.

[Ambivalent] Well, I went to do the homework, but then it occurred to me that I shouldn’t
try to reduce my worry too much. I mean it’s stressful, but there are times it actually helps
me stay on top of things . . . to be accountable.

[Curious] I’m still trying to get the hang of identifying my thoughts. What should I plan for
next week?

[Defeated] You know, I’ve felt a lot better these past few weeks, and I honestly wonder if
it’s because I stopped doing those exercises you gave me. I mean, maybe writing down
my thoughts and trying to relax is making me worse . . . maybe this is just who I am, and
this is the best that I can feel, and I just need to learn to live with that.

[Nervous, deflecting from exposure task] Oh, I forgot to tell you that I might be switching
jobs. Maybe we should talk about that instead today?
[Ashamed] I did some of what we talked about last week but forgot the forms.

[Nervous] I have a hard time with organization, so I’m worried about doing all of the
homework correctly.
[Panicking] Oh my god . . . Oh my god . . . I’m dying! I can’t breathe! Help me!

[Frustrated] Well, I’m not really sure about it, but I guess I’ll give the thought record
another shot if you think that’s best.

[Curious, after emotion monitoring homework was assigned at the end of the previous
session] Where should we start today?
[Nervous] You’re the expert, so just tell me what to do today
[Discouraged] I’ve still been pretty down, I guess. I spent most of the week in bed.

[Anxious] I know I sometimes think in extremes, but what if the worst thing actually did
happen? It could.

[Curious] I’m not sure about an agenda. With my other therapist, I just kind of talked about
whatever was on my mind.

[Curious] I’m still trying to get the hang of identifying my thoughts. Should I plan for
anything next week?

[Nervous] The things that you’re saying make sense. I can see how this way of working
would be helpful to other people, but I’m not sure it is a good fit for me.

[Frustrated] To be honest, the last couple of sessions I’ve been confused by our focus on
my challenges. My family says I should just stay positive, smile more, and not think about
anything negative. Do we have to discuss my challenges?

[Annoyed] How will focusing more on these negative thoughts and feelings make me feel
better rather than just feel worse?
[Excited] You won’t believe what happened this week!

[Angry] The exposure you assigned last week was a disaster. I had a panic attack on the
train, and everyone stared at me. So embarrassing. It’s your fault because you told me
to do it.

[Impatient] Wait a minute . . . you’re saying if I can’t fall asleep, then I need to get out of
bed and stop trying to sleep?

[Irritated] Well, I guess the homework you’re suggesting makes some sense, but I’m
also easily irritated lately . . . especially when things are unclear for me and when they’re
overwhelming.

[Anxious] I really want to try testing some of my assumptions about what people think of
me, but I’m just not sure I’m ready.

[Frustrated] You think I should set up some “little rewards” to start feeling less depressed.
That seems kind of embarrassing and infantilizing.

[Afraid] I’ve had bad experiences in therapy before, and I’m unsure if it’s really helpful. How
is this going to be different?

[Concerned] I really need to know why I am the way I am now. I think understanding my
past and childhood is really important, but it sounds like this approach doesn’t get into
any of that?

[Apprehensive] I successfully did the homework! However, it made me very nervous, so I
had a few drinks beforehand. This is OK, right? I hope you don’t judge my drinking, like my
wife and boss do.

[Frustrated] I just don’t think you’re equipped to help me. The whole “cognitive triad”
thing, or whatever you called it, seems bogus.
[Nervous] I’ve never been in therapy before. Do we just talk about my past or upbringing?
[Curious] How long will this take?
[Dismissive] I’m not sure this is the best use of my time today.

[Frustrated] My boss’s evaluation of me was devastating. I’m at a loss. There is no other
perspective on this.

[Angry] My partner cheated on me. And, no, there is no alternative explanation, so stop
asking that! He cheated, so our relationship was a lie!
[Dismissive] I’m not sure this is the right thing for me.

[Anxious] I did the measure you asked me to fill out. Honestly, I think I might have rated
you lower than usual, but I’m not sure I want to talk about it.

[Crying] My partner broke up with me today. I know it’s stupid, but I really thought we
were going to get married.
[Nervous] I’ve never been in therapy before. What do we talk about here?

[Anxious] I’ve learned some new things. But I still feel tense all the time. I can’t have a
conversation with anyone without lashing out. I feel on edge and still can’t really relax.
[Sad] I know I’m a terrible mother.

[Anxious] I know the plan was to review my monitoring, but I learned yesterday that I might
lose my job.
[Ashamed] I was only able to do part of what we talked about last week.

[Angry] You don’t understand. I want to stop feeling sad, not practice feeling sad. I’m
already pretty freaking great at feeling bad. So, I really don’t need more practice at that!
[Anxious] I’m not sure I’m ready to do this on my own.

[Angry] Honestly, I just don’t see how you can help me. I mean, sure, if I had your life
maybe I could sit around and relax at the end of everyday too, but I don’t! In my life, I don’t
get to relax. So, I just don’t see how you’re going to be able to fix that for me.
[Weeping] I just don’t think I can do this homework on my own.
[Nervous] What do we do next with this exposure thing?

[Panicking] After touching all of the bathroom walls with millions of germs—I am going to
wash my hands immediately! I get the point of exposure, but it’s crazy not to wash your
hands after what we just did.
[Weeping] I just can’t imagine anything changing. I feel so hopeless.

[Frustrated] I’m just not getting it. I don’t understand what you’re asking me to do for the
homework.

[Relieved] I’m glad you could see my reluctance about cognitive behavioral therapy! I think
it started to feel more like a class than a treatment, which was unhelpful. I do want to work
on feeling better—and thinking better [laughs]—but sometimes I don’t have a clear agenda
or direction. In those times, just taking some space to talk freely helps me a lot.

[Exasperated] I feel like you’ve been hearing me wrong since we started. You don’t seem
to understand what I mean. Are you even listening?
[Nervous] My partner wants us to talk about something today.

[Assertive] I do feel bad for missing sessions. I need to be in therapy. I need to get this
stress under control. I just don’t think we’ve attacked it the right way.
[Curious] How does therapy work?

[Flustered] I actually need to be out the door right now. Is there anything that I should do
before our next session?

[Surprised] That was a really abrupt ending last session. I know we only have an hour,
but I was kind of in the middle of something. That’s been on my mind ever since. I even
considered not coming today . . . I guess I’ve been a little pissed off about it.
[Angry] What we’re doing in here is so stupid!

[Shaking and teary] I’m really embarrassed . . . I kind of lied to you about what I thought
I could handle in here. I didn’t want to disappoint you or make you feel like this is a waste
of time.

[Agitated] I’d go into what happened back then, but I know that we focus on the present
in this therapy.
[Frustrated] I cut myself this week. I don’t know why I harm myself like I do.

[Frustrated] Why do you just keep asking questions, over and over again? It’s really
frustrating not to get anything more direct from you.

[Matter of fact] I think my problems partly stem from the racism and disrespect that
I experience at work.

[Angry] Actually, no, I don’t want to set an agenda. I don’t think that I want to keep doing
this stuff. I just don’t see the point!
